memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then the Lord said to Moses, 'Leave this place, you and the people you brought up out of Egypt, and go up to the land I promised on oath to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, saying, "I will give it to your descendants."'" - Exod 33:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After the golden calf, we might expect God's first words to be a cancellation. Instead, He says: go up to the land I promised.

The promise still stands. Not because Israel deserved it — they had just proved they did not — but because God had sworn it to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob long before this generation existed. God's promises rest on God's faithfulness, not ours.

Still, notice the sting in that phrase: "the people you brought up out of Egypt." God had said the same thing in the previous chapter. It is not a slip. Something in the relationship has been wounded, and God speaks of it plainly rather than pretending all is well.

That combination is worth sitting with. God keeps His word and He does not pretend. He will not abandon His purposes, and He will not act as though sin never happened. Both things are true at once.

For us, the ground of every promise is Christ. "For no matter how many promises God has made, they are 'Yes' in Christ" (2 Cor 1:20). If you have failed badly, God's purposes for you are not undone. But do not mistake His faithfulness for indifference. He is calling you back into closeness, not just forward into blessing.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you believe God's promises rest on His faithfulness rather than your performance?
2. Is there a distance between you and God you have been ignoring?
3. What has God called you to that you stopped pursuing after a failure?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that Your promises do not collapse when I do. Restore what my sin has damaged, and lead me on. Amen.
